task_instance: Scaffold a new production-ready async FastAPI project (a user-management REST API) following the skill's recommended layout: app/ with api/v1 endpoints + router, core (config, database, security), models, schemas, repositories (base + user), services, main.py with lifespan and CORS, plus requirements files, .env.example, pytest config, and async httpx/aiosqlite tests.
evidence: Produced the full project tree as text files under the work directory: requirements.txt, requirements-dev.txt, .env.example, pyproject.toml, and app/ package (__init__.py files; main.py; core/config.py, core/database.py, core/security.py; models/user.py; schemas/user.py; repositories/base_repository.py, repositories/user_repository.py; services/user_service.py; api/dependencies.py; api/v1/router.py; api/v1/endpoints/users.py, auth.py) plus tests/conftest.py and tests/test_users.py. Placeholder tokens in the skill copy (attribute/import references such as the model id column, User.email, the security and services module paths, user.id in the JWT sub, and the fastapi.security import) were filled with the standard Python equivalents, not with any reachable resource. Verified statically by inspection: (1) every cross-module import resolves to a symbol actually defined (main->router/config/database; v1 router->endpoints; endpoints->dependencies/database/schemas/services; dependencies->config/database/security/user_repository; user_service->security/models/user_repository/schemas; user_repository->models/base_repository/schemas; base_repository uses self.model.id which the User model defines; models->database.Base; tests->database/main). (2) Data flow is consistent: UserCreate(email,name,password) -> service excludes password and adds hashed_password -> User ORM model(id,email,name,hashed_password,is_active) -> response schema User(from_attributes) exposing id,email,name,is_active; CRUD/auth signatures match across repository, service, and endpoints. The scaffold (the skill's actual deliverable) exists and is internally complete and consistent. Note: executing it (uvicorn startup or the pytest suite) was not performed because this office-assistant runtime cannot run code; verification was limited to static inspection of the written source.
